title: Policing the Ellington band when Duke would not
summary: In Duke's band Cootie hollered at Hodges and Bigard if they played wrong or fooled around, since Duke never spoke.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: No. I can remember, Cootie, on record sessions with the band, with the Ellington band. I can remember you getting so mad toward the end of a session. Sometimes maybe Sonny was fooling around or something. And Duke wasn't doing anything, wasn't stepping in. And I can remember you getting so mad, and getting down from the stand and shouting at everybody, and saying, 'Let's get on and get this in and do
this." Do you remember ? You used to do that.
Oh, yeah. I used to do that.
I mean, I don't know whether you used to do it on the job, but you did do it on the sessions.
I used to do it on the job, too.
Did you?

Yeah. If Johnny or Barney or any of them were in an argument, wasn't playing the music right, I'd holler at them. Because Duke would never say nothing to them. I'd be the one that had taken over that spot.
No kidding?
Yeah.
Well, how did that go down?
Well, I didn't care.
Yeah.
As long as the music would be played right.
Yeah.
If they wasn't playing the music right, I would tell them and holler at them.
Well, it went down all right, because, I mean, the knew that's how it was, didn't they?
Yeah. That's the way it was, yeah.
It had to be that way.
Yeah.
Yeah. And also, for people, not only that it wasn't being played right, but people were kidding around on the job.
Uh-huh.
And it was going on too long. Right?
Yeah. Uh-huh.

Yeah. While we're just on that subject, because we didn't get into it when we were talking about the band, what about -- I mean, the things that used to go on in that reed section, what about like Barney and Johnny who shouldered one against the other, and not really even talking to each other, actually. For long periods. Am I not right?
Yeah. Well -- and sometimes it used to interfere with the music.
Well, that's what I mean.
And that's the time I would come in. Duke wouldn't say nothing, but I would come in and say something.
Well, I mean, what would you do?
Just like the band belonged to me, then.
(Laughter)
If they wasn't playing that music right.
I mean, it's really -- how are you going to handle a section with two guys in the section that aren't even speaking, you know. It's pretty bad, isn't it?
I'd get them on the ball.
You would.

Yeah. They cursed me about sometimes. Other times, they'd let me go. But I didn't care, you know. What would happen. After I spoke my word, if they wasn't playing that music right. Johnny or Barney, any of them in there. If they was doing something wrong. Of course that wasn't Duke's idea, to say nothing to nobody. And so I'd take it on my shoulders to speak to them about it.
I guess, you know, that was a good thing, as far as Duke was concerned.
Yeah.
